title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 9
paragraphs: These were the ships of the Ionians; and of the barbarians the number of ships was six hundred. When these too had come to the Milesian coast and their whole land-army was also on hand, then the commanders of the Persians, being informed of the number of Ionian ships, were struck with fear that they would not be able to overcome them, and thus on the one hand would not be able to conquer Miletus for lack of command of the sea, and at the same time would run the risk of being punished by Darius. Reflecting on these things, they gathered together the tyrants of the Ionians who were exiles with the Medes, having been deposed from their governments by Aristagoras the Milesian, and who happened to be then taking part in the expedition against Miletus. Of these men they called together those who were present and spoke to them as follows: “Ionians, now let each of you show himself a benefactor of the king's house—that is, let each try to detach his own countrymen from the alliance. Make your proposals, promising at the same time that they shall suffer nothing unpleasant for their revolt; neither their temples nor their private houses shall be burned, nor shall they have any worse treatment than they had before. But if they will not do so, and persist in entering into a contest with us, threaten them and tell them this, which in truth will happen to them: if they are worsted in the fight, they shall be reduced to slavery; we will make their sons eunuchs, we will remove their maidens to Bactria, and we will hand their land over to others.”
